title: Generated Go code emits unused expression statement when translating comma operator
body:
When translating a C comma expression with multiple operands, c2go generates an unused expression as a standalone Go statement:
```go
c * int32(2)
```
However, Go does not allow this kind of unused expression statement, so the generated program fails to compile.
The generated code also takes the address of a non-addressable arithmetic expression:
```go
tempVar := &(c + int32(10))
```
but the main issue here is the unused expression emitted from the discarded operand of the comma expression.
**To Reproduce**
```c
#include <stdio.h>

int main(void) {
    int c = 0;
    int result = (c = 1, c * 2, c + 10);

    printf("%d %d\n", c, result);
    return 0;
}
```
The generated Go code contains:
```go
func main() {
        var c int32 = int32(0)
        var result int32 = func() int32 {
                c = int32(1)
                c * int32(2)
                tempVar := &(c + int32(10))
                return *tempVar
        }()
        noarch.Printf((&[]byte("%d %d\n\x00")[0]), c, result)
        return
}
```
**Observed Behavior**
```
# command-line-arguments
./test.go:168:3: c * int32(2) (value of type int32) is not used
./test.go:169:16: invalid operation: cannot take address of c + int32(10) (value of type int32)
```
The main invalid generated code is:
```go
c * int32(2)
```
